result.title: Local Diagnostics of Learned Event Representations for Anomaly Detection at the HL-LHC
result.summary: Anomaly detection, the identification of collision events that deviate from Standard Model expectations, is one of the most promising model-agnostic strategies for new-physics searches at the Large Hadron Collider. Searching for rare events in learned low-dimensional representations removes the need to commit to hand-crafted observables a priori, but sacrifices the immediate physical interpretation those observables provide. For anomaly detection to enter a discovery pipeline, flagged events must therefore be diagnosed locally, both to distinguish potential new physics from mismodeling or detector effects and to identify observables for targeted follow-up searches. We evaluate supervised and self-supervised neural embedding strategies on COLLIDE-2V, a 750-million-event dataset simulated under realistic High-Luminosity LHC conditions, using the reconstruction error of an autoencoder trained in the learned latent space as the anomaly score. Across the configurations and benchmark signals considered, supervised objectives, which exploit simulation process labels during training, generally outperform their self-supervised counterparts and, in their best configurations, improve on an autoencoder trained directly on kinematic features, raising the signal efficiency at 10% background acceptance on all held-out processes. We further introduce a local diagnostic pipeline that fits a Gaussian Mixture Model to the SM latent space, profiles each component through high-level observables without process labels, localizes the flagged events, and ranks observables by their local discriminating power. The ranking recovers the defining kinematics of the held-out processes, while correlating the anomaly score with the same observables quantifies how closely the score tracks them, revealing cases where the most discriminating observable is not the one the score follows most closely.

AI.brief_summary: 在 COLLIDE-2V 的 7.5 亿模拟 LHC 事件上比较监督与自监督神经嵌入的异常检测，以 latent 空间自编码器重构误差作异常分数，并提出基于 GMM 的局部诊断流程定位被标记事件、按局部区分力排序高维观测量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「异常分数跟随哪个观测量」与「哪个观测量最具区分力」分开诊断的做法，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 内容是否真被答案使用、以及内容与深度/位置影响的诊断提供类比线索，需进一步核查。
